sanskrit: evaṃ mṛtyuṃ jāyamānaṃ viditvā; jñāne tiṣṭhan na bibhetīha mṛtyoḥ vinaśyate viṣaye tasya mṛtyur; mṛtyor yathā viṣayaṃ prāpya martyaḥ
english: Having understood death as it arises, he who stands firm in knowledge does not fear death here. Death is destroyed in its own domain, just as a mortal, upon entering the realm of death, is destroyed.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca ye 'smin dharmān nācarantīha ke cit; tathā dharmān ke cid ihācaranti dharmaḥ pāpena pratihanyate sma; utāho dharmaḥ pratihanti pāpam
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Some in this world do not practice righteousness here, while others practice righteousness here. Is righteousness obstructed by sin, or does righteousness overcome sin?

sanskrit: sanatsujāta uvāca ubhayam eva tatropabhujyate phalaṃ; dharmasyaivetarasya ca dharmeṇādharmaṃ praṇudatīha vidvān; dharmo balīyān iti tasya viddhi
english: Sanatsujata said: In that case the fruit of both is experienced — of righteousness and of its opposite. The wise man repels unrighteousness by means of righteousness here. Know this: righteousness is the stronger of the two.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca yān imān āhuḥ svasya dharmasya lokān; dvijātīnāṃ puṇyakṛtāṃ sanātanān teṣāṃ parikramān kathayantas tato 'nyān; naitad vidvan naiva kṛtaṃ ca karma
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Those worlds of one's own righteousness which they speak of — the eternal worlds of twice-born men of meritorious deeds — those who tell of their courses and then speak of others have not done this deed, O wise one, nor has it truly been done.

sanskrit: sanatsujāta uvāca yeṣāṃ bale na vispardhā bale balavatām iva te brāhmaṇā itaḥ pretya svargaloke prakāśate
english: Sanatsujata said: Those brahmanas who do not compete in strength as if rivaling the strong — they shine in the heavenly world after departing from here.

sanskrit: yatra manyeta bhūyiṣṭhaṃ prāvṛṣīva tṛṇolapam annaṃ pānaṃ ca brāhmaṇas taj jīvan nānusaṃjvaret
english: Where a brahmana should think of food and drink as being as plentiful as grass and fuel during the rainy season — living there, he should not grieve over it.

sanskrit: yatrākathayamānasya prayacchaty aśivaṃ bhayam atiriktam ivākurvan sa śreyān netaro janaḥ
english: Where one, without boasting, gives away what is inauspicious and fearful, acting as though doing something superfluous — that person is better, not the other.

sanskrit: yo vākathayamānasya ātmānaṃ nānusaṃjvaret brahmasvaṃ nopabhuñjed vā tadannaṃ saṃmataṃ satām
english: One who, without boasting, does not grieve over himself, who does not enjoy the property of brahmanas — that food is approved by the good.

sanskrit: yathā svaṃ vāntam aśnāti śvā vai nityam abhūtaye evaṃ te vāntam aśnanti svavīryasyopajīvanāt
english: Just as a dog always eats what it has vomited, to its own destruction, so those who live by exploiting their own prowess eat what has been vomited.

sanskrit: nityam ajñātacaryā me iti manyeta brāhmaṇaḥ jñātīnāṃ tu vasan madhye naiva vidyeta kiṃ cana
english: A brahmana should always think: "My conduct is unknown." But dwelling in the midst of kinsmen, nothing whatsoever would be known of him.

sanskrit: ko hy evam antarātmānaṃ brāhmaṇo hantum arhati tasmād dhi kiṃ cit kṣatriya brahmāvasati paśyati
english: For who deserves to slay such a brahmana in his inner self? Therefore, O kshatriya, Brahman dwells in something and perceives it.

sanskrit: aśrāntaḥ syād anādānāt saṃmato nirupadravaḥ śiṣṭo na śiṣṭavat sa syād brāhmaṇo brahmavit kaviḥ
english: He should be untiring through non-acquisition, respected and free from affliction. Disciplined, yet not posturing as disciplined — such should be the brahmana who knows Brahman, the wise seer.

sanskrit: anāḍhyā mānuṣe vitte āḍhyā vedeṣu ye dvijāḥ te durdharṣā duṣprakampyā vidyāt tān brahmaṇas tanum
english: Those twice-born who are not wealthy in human riches but are wealthy in the Vedas — they are hard to assail, hard to shake. Know them as the body of Brahman.

sanskrit: sarvān sviṣṭakṛto devān vidyād ya iha kaś cana na samāno brāhmaṇasya yasmin prayatate svayam
english: Whoever here knows all the gods who have performed proper sacrifices — there is no equal to the brahmana in whom Brahman strives of its own accord.

sanskrit: yam aprayatamānaṃ tu mānayanti sa mānitaḥ na mānyamāno manyeta nāmānād abhisaṃjvaret
english: He who is honored even when not striving to be — he is truly honored. The one truly worthy of honor should not consider himself disrespected, nor should he grieve over disrespect.

sanskrit: vidvāṃso mānayantīha iti manyeta mānitaḥ adharmaviduṣo mūḍhā lokaśāstraviśāradāḥ na mānyaṃ mānayiṣyanti iti manyed amānitaḥ
english: The one who is honored should think: "The learned honor me here." The one who is not honored should think: "The fools ignorant of righteousness, though skilled in worldly scriptures, will not honor the one worthy of honor."

sanskrit: na vai mānaṃ ca maunaṃ ca sahitau carataḥ sadā ayaṃ hi loko mānasya asau mānasya tad viduḥ
english: Indeed, honor and silence do not go together always. This world belongs to honor, and that world too belongs to honor — so the wise know.

sanskrit: śrīḥ sukhasyeha saṃvāsaḥ sā cāpi paripanthinī brāhmī sudurlabhā śrīr hi prajñāhīnena kṣatriya
english: Prosperity is the companion of happiness here, and yet she is also an obstacle. The Brahmic prosperity is very hard to attain, O kshatriya, for one lacking in wisdom.

sanskrit: dvārāṇi tasyā hi vadanti santo; bahuprakārāṇi durāvarāṇi satyārjave hrīr damaśaucavidyāḥ; ṣaṇmānamohapratibādhanāni
english: The good declare her doors to be many in kind and hard to enter: truth, honesty, modesty, self-restraint, purity, and knowledge — six that obstruct pride and delusion.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca ṛco yajūṃṣy adhīte yaḥ sāmavedaṃ ca yo dvijaḥ pāpāni kurvan pāpena lipyate na sa lipyate
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: He who, being a twice-born, studies the Rig verses, the Yajus, and the Sāmaveda — when he commits sins, is he tainted by sin or is he not tainted?

sanskrit: sanatsujāta uvāca nainaṃ sāmāny ṛco vāpi na yajūṃṣi vicakṣaṇa trāyante karmaṇaḥ pāpān na te mithyā bravīmy aham
english: Sanatsujata said: The Sāmans, nor even the Rig verses, nor the Yajus, O discerning one, protect him from sinful deeds. I do not speak falsely to you.

sanskrit: na chandāṃsi vṛjināt tārayanti; māyāvinaṃ māyayā vartamānam nīḍaṃ śakuntā iva jātapakṣāś; chandāṃsy enaṃ prajahaty antakāle
english: The Vedic meters do not carry across one who practices deceit through deceit — as fledglings leave the nest when their wings have grown, the meters abandon him at the time of death.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca na ced vedā vedavidaṃ śaktās trātuṃ vicakṣaṇa atha kasmāt pralāpo 'yaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ sanātanaḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: If the Vedas are not capable of saving even the knower of the Vedas, O discerning one, then why does this eternal teaching of the brahmanas persist?

sanskrit: sanatsujāta uvāca asmiṃl loke tapas taptaṃ phalam anyatra dṛśyate brāhmaṇānām ime lokā ṛddhe tapasi saṃyatāḥ
english: Sanatsujata said: Austerity practiced in this world bears fruit seen in another. These worlds of brahmanas are attained when austerity is abundant and restraint is observed.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca kathaṃ samṛddham apy ṛddhaṃ tapo bhavati kevalam sanatsujāta tad brūhi yathā vidyāma tad vayam
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: How does austerity become complete and fully abundant, O Sanatsujata? Tell me that, so that we may understand it.

sanskrit: sanatsujāta uvāca krodhādayo dvādaśa yasya doṣās; tathā nṛśaṃsādi ṣaḍ atra rājan dharmādayo dvādaśa cātatānāḥ; śāstre guṇā ye viditā dvijānām
english: Sanatsujata said: Anger and eleven other faults, and the six beginning with cruelty, O king — and the twelve qualities beginning with righteousness that are well known to the twice-born in the scriptures —

sanskrit: krodhaḥ kāmo lobhamohau vivitsā;kṛpāsūyā mānaśokau spṛhā ca īrṣyā jugupsā ca manuṣyadoṣā; varjyāḥ sadā dvādaśaite nareṇa
english: Anger, desire, greed, delusion, the wish to obtain, grief, envy, pride, sorrow, longing, jealousy, and disgust — these twelve faults of humans should always be avoided by a man.

sanskrit: ekaikam ete rājendra manuṣyān paryupāsate lipsamāno 'ntaraṃ teṣāṃ mṛgāṇām iva lubdhakaḥ
english: Each one of these, O king of kings, stalks human beings one by one, seeking an opening among them, like a hunter among deer.

sanskrit: vikatthanaḥ spṛhayālur manasvī; bibhrat kopaṃ capalo 'rakṣaṇaś ca ete prāptāḥ ṣaṇ narān pāpadharmān; prakurvate nota santaḥ sudurge
english: The boastful, the envious, the arrogant, one who harbors anger, the fickle, and the unguarded — these six, when they prevail, lead men into evil conduct. The good do not do this, even in dire straits.

sanskrit: saṃbhogasaṃvid dviṣam edhamāno; dattānutāpī kṛpaṇo 'balīyān vargapraśaṃsī vanitāsu dveṣṭā; ete 'pare sapta nṛśaṃsadharmāḥ
english: One who grows in enmity through shared enjoyment, one who regrets what he has given, the miser, the weak, the praiser of factions, and the one who despises women — these are the other seven cruel traits.

sanskrit: dharmaś ca satyaṃ ca damas tapaś ca; amātsaryaṃ hrīs titikṣānasūyā yajñaś ca dānaṃ ca dhṛtiḥ śrutaṃ ca; mahāvratā dvādaśa brāhmaṇasya
english: Righteousness, truth, self-restraint, austerity, absence of jealousy, modesty, forbearance, freedom from envy, sacrifice, charity, steadfastness, and sacred learning — these are the twelve great vows of a brahmana.

sanskrit: yas tv etebhyaḥ pravased dvādaśebhyaḥ; sarvām apīmāṃ pṛthivīṃ praśiṣyāt tribhir dvābhyām ekato vā viśiṣṭo; nāsya svam astīti sa veditavyaḥ
english: But one who has fallen away from these twelve — he would instruct the entire earth; distinguished in three, two, or even one — know that he has nothing of his own.

sanskrit: damas tyāgo 'pramādaś ca eteṣv amṛtam āhitam tāni satyamukhāny āhur brāhmaṇā ye manīṣiṇaḥ
english: Self-restraint, renunciation, and vigilance — in these the immortal is established. Those wise brahmanas call them the gateways to truth.

sanskrit: damo 'ṣṭādaśadoṣaḥ syāt pratikūlaṃ kṛtākṛte anṛtaṃ cābhyasūyā ca kāmārthau ca tathā spṛhā
english: Self-restraint has eighteen faults: acting contrary to what is done and undone, falsehood, envy, desire, self-interest, and longing —

sanskrit: krodhaḥ śokas tathā tṛṣṇā lobhaḥ paiśunyam eva ca matsaraś ca vivitsā ca paritāpas tathā ratiḥ
english: Anger, sorrow, thirst, greed, slander, ill-will, the desire to acquire, anguish, and attachment —

sanskrit: apasmāraḥ sātivādas tathā saṃbhāvanātmani etair vimukto doṣair yaḥ sa damaḥ sadbhir ucyate
english: Forgetfulness, excessive speech, and conceit about oneself — one who is freed from these faults is called self-restraint by the good.

sanskrit: śreyāṃs tu ṣaḍvidhas tyāgaḥ priyaṃ prāpya na hṛṣyati apriye tu samutpanne vyathāṃ jātu na cārcchati
english: But renunciation is superior in six ways: on obtaining what is dear, one does not rejoice; and when the unpleasant arises, one does not ever reach distress.

sanskrit: iṣṭān dārāṃś ca putrāṃś ca na cānyaṃ yad vaco bhavet arhate yācamānāya pradeyaṃ tad vaco bhavet apy avācyaṃ vadaty eva sa tṛtīyo guṇaḥ smṛtaḥ
english: Beloved wives and sons — and whatever speech is appropriate, whatever should be given to one who begs, that speech should be spoken. Even what should not be spoken, he speaks nonetheless — that is remembered as the third quality.

sanskrit: tyaktair dravyair yo bhavati nopayuṅkte ca kāmataḥ na ca karmasu tad dhīnaḥ śiṣyabuddhir naro yathā sarvair eva guṇair yukto dravyavān api yo bhavet
english: One who exists with things given up and does not use them through desire, who is not diminished in actions on that account — like a student in mind — such a man who is endowed with all these qualities, even if he possesses wealth, would be so.

sanskrit: apramādo 'ṣṭadoṣaḥ syāt tān doṣān parivarjayet indriyebhyaś ca pañcabhyo manasaś caiva bhārata atītānāgatebhyaś ca mukto hy etaiḥ sukhī bhavet
english: Vigilance has eight faults that should be abandoned: from the five senses and from the mind, O Bhārata, and from past and future — one freed from these becomes happy.

sanskrit: doṣair etair vimuktaṃ tu guṇair etaiḥ samanvitam etat samṛddham apy ṛddhaṃ tapo bhavati kevalam yan māṃ pṛcchasi rājendra kiṃ bhūyaḥ śrotum icchasi
english: That which is freed from these faults and endowed with these qualities — this is the complete and fully abundant austerity alone, about which you ask me, O king. What more do you wish to hear?

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca ākhyānapañcamair vedair bhūyiṣṭhaṃ kathyate janaḥ tathaivānye caturvedās trivedāś ca tathāpare
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: By the Vedas with the epics as fifth, most people are largely described. Likewise there are others with four Vedas, others with three Vedas —

sanskrit: dvivedāś caikavedāś ca anṛcaś ca tathāpare teṣāṃ tu katamaḥ sa syād yam ahaṃ veda brāhmaṇam
english: And those with two Vedas, those with one Veda, and yet others with no Rig verses at all. Among them, who is the one I should know as a true brahmana?

sanskrit: sanatsujāta uvāca ekasya vedasyājñānād vedās te bahavo 'bhavan satyasyaikasya rājendra satye kaś cid avasthitaḥ evaṃ vedam anutsādya prajñāṃ mahati kurvate
english: Sanatsujata said: Through not knowing the one Veda, those many Vedas came to be. Of the one truth, O king, one who is established in truth — thus, having set aside the Veda, they place wisdom in the great.

sanskrit: dānam adhyayanaṃ yajño lobhād etat pravartate satyāt pracyavamānānāṃ saṃkalpo vitatho bhavet
english: Charity, study, and sacrifice — these proceed from greed. For those who fall away from truth, their intention becomes fruitless.

sanskrit: tato yajñaḥ pratāyeta satyasyaivāvadhāraṇāt manasānyasya bhavati vācānyasyota karmaṇā saṃkalpasiddhaḥ puruṣaḥ saṃkalpān adhitiṣṭhati
english: Then sacrifice extends from the very firm grasp of truth. One whose mind is different, whose speech is different, and whose action is different — a man accomplished in resolve stands above mere resolutions.

sanskrit: anaibhṛtyena vai tasya dīkṣitavratam ācaret nāmaitad dhātunirvṛttaṃ satyam eva satāṃ param jñānaṃ vai nāma pratyakṣaṃ parokṣaṃ jāyate tapaḥ
english: One should practice the vow of initiation without servility. This indeed — established in its root — is the name; truth alone is the highest for the good. Knowledge is indeed what is called the direct; austerity is what is generated as the indirect.

sanskrit: vidyād bahu paṭhantaṃ tu bahupāṭhīti brāhmaṇam tasmāt kṣatriya mā maṃsthā jalpitenaiva brāhmaṇam ya eva satyān nāpaiti sa jñeyo brāhmaṇas tvayā
english: One should know that one who reads much is merely a brahmana by much-reading. Therefore, O kshatriya, do not regard someone as a brahmana by mere chatter. Only one who never departs from truth — know him as the true brahmana.

sanskrit: chandāṃsi nāma kṣatriya tāny atharvā; jagau purastād ṛṣisarga eṣaḥ chandovidas te ya u tān adhītya; na vedyavedasya vidur na vedyam
english: The Vedic meters, O kshatriya — Atharvan sang those first; this is the stream of seers. Those who know the meters and have studied them do not know the knowable of the Veda, nor the knowable.

sanskrit: na vedānāṃ veditā kaś cid asti; kaś cid vedān budhyate vāpi rājan yo veda vedān na sa veda vedyaṃ; satye sthito yas tu sa veda vedyam
english: There is no one who is truly the knower of the Vedas; someone may comprehend the Vedas, O king. But one who knows the Vedas does not know the knowable — only one established in truth knows the knowable.

sanskrit: abhijānāmi brāhmaṇam ākhyātāraṃ vicakṣaṇam yaś chinnavicikitsaḥ sann ācaṣṭe sarvasaṃśayān
english: I recognize the brahmana as the wise declarer who, with all doubt cut away, elucidates all uncertainties.

sanskrit: tasya paryeṣaṇaṃ gacchet prācīnaṃ nota dakṣiṇam nārvācīnaṃ kutas tiryaṅ nādiśaṃ tu kathaṃ cana
english: In search of him one should go eastward, not southward, not toward the near, how much less diagonally, and in no direction in any manner whatsoever.

sanskrit: tūṣṇīṃbhūta upāsīta na ceṣṭen manasā api abhyāvarteta brahmāsya antarātmani vai śritam
english: Having become silent, one should attend, not even striving with the mind. Brahman should be returned to — it is indeed lodged in the inner self.

sanskrit: maunād dhi sa munir bhavati nāraṇyavasanān muniḥ akṣaraṃ tat tu yo veda sa muniḥ śreṣṭha ucyate
english: A sage is truly a sage because of silence, not because of dwelling in the forest. But one who knows that imperishable — he is called the supreme sage.

sanskrit: sarvārthānāṃ vyākaraṇād vaiyākaraṇa ucyate pratyakṣadarśī lokānāṃ sarvadarśī bhaven naraḥ
english: Through the analysis of all meanings one is called a grammarian. One who sees the worlds directly becomes one who sees all.

sanskrit: satye vai brāhmaṇas tiṣṭhan brahma paśyati kṣatriya vedānāṃ cānupūrvyeṇa etad vidvan bravīmi te
english: A brahmana standing in truth truly sees Brahman, O kshatriya, in the sequential order of the Vedas. Knowing this, I declare it to you.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca sanatsujāta yad imāṃ parārthāṃ; brāhmīṃ vācaṃ pravadasi viśvarūpām parāṃ hi kāmeṣu sudurlabhāṃ kathāṃ; tad brūhi me vākyam etat kumāra
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: O Sanatsujata, since you speak this all-pervading brahmic speech for the sake of another — this supreme discourse, so very rare among desires — declare that word to me, O youth.

sanskrit: sanatsujāta uvāca naitad brahma tvaramāṇena labhyaṃ; yan māṃ pṛcchasy abhihṛṣyasy atīva avyaktavidyām abhidhāsye purāṇīṃ; buddhyā ca teṣāṃ brahmacaryeṇa siddhām
english: Sanatsujata said: This Brahman is not to be attained by one in a hurry — you ask me about it and are overly excited. I shall expound the ancient unmanifest knowledge, perfected by understanding and by the brahmacharya of those who have realized it.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca avyaktavidyām iti yat sanātanīṃ; bravīṣi tvaṃ brahmacaryeṇa siddhām anārabhyā vasatīhārya kāle; kathaṃ brāhmaṇyam amṛtatvaṃ labheta
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: This eternal unmanifest knowledge which you speak of — perfected by brahmacharya, not to be begun here at just any time, O noble one — how then does one attain brahminhood and immortality?

sanskrit: sanatsujāta uvāca ye 'smiṃl loke vijayantīha kāmān; brāhmīṃ sthitim anutitikṣamāṇāḥ ta ātmānaṃ nirharantīha dehān; muñjād iṣīkām iva sattvasaṃsthāḥ
english: Sanatsujata said: Those who conquer desires in this world, who endure seeking the brahmic state — they extract the self from the bodies here, established in pure being, like the reed from the munja grass.

sanskrit: śarīram etau kurutaḥ pitā mātā ca bhārata ācāryaśāstā yā jātiḥ sā satyā sājarāmarā
english: The father and mother make this body, O Bhārata. The teacher-instructor gives birth to a true birth — that birth is real, that birth is ageless and immortal.

sanskrit: ācāryayonim iha ye praviśya; bhūtvā garbhaṃ brahmacaryaṃ caranti ihaiva te śāstrakārā bhavanti; prahāya dehaṃ paramaṃ yānti yogam
english: Those who enter here into the womb of the teacher, becoming as an embryo and practicing brahmacharya — they become makers of scripture in this very world; casting off the body, they attain the supreme yoga.

sanskrit: ya āvṛṇoty avitathena karṇā;vṛtaṃ kurvann amṛtaṃ saṃprayacchan taṃ manyeta pitaraṃ mātaraṃ ca; tasmai na druhyet kṛtam asya jānan
english: One who covers the ears with truth, making them veiled, and grants the immortal — him one should regard as both father and mother. One who knows what has been done by him should not wrong him.

sanskrit: guruṃ śiṣyo nityam abhimanyamānaḥ; svādhyāyam icchec chucir apramattaḥ mānaṃ na kuryān na dadhīta roṣam; eṣa prathamo brahmacaryasya pādaḥ
english: A student who always honors the teacher, who is pure and diligent in desiring self-study, who does not act with pride and does not harbor anger — this is the first quarter of brahmacharya.

sanskrit: ācāryasya priyaṃ kuryāt prāṇair api dhanair api karmaṇā manasā vācā dvitīyaḥ pāda ucyate
english: One should do what is dear to the teacher, even at the cost of one's life, even with wealth, in deed, in mind, and in speech — this is called the second quarter.

sanskrit: samā gurau yathā vṛttir gurupatnyāṃ tathā bhavet yathoktakārī priyakṛt tṛtīyaḥ pāda ucyate
english: Just as one's conduct toward the teacher, so should it be toward the teacher's wife. One who does what is instructed and is pleasing to them — this is called the third quarter.

sanskrit: nācāryāyehopakṛtvā pravādaṃ; prājñaḥ kurvīta naitad ahaṃ karomi itīva manyeta na bhāṣayeta; sa vai caturtho brahmacaryasya pādaḥ
english: Having done a service for the teacher, the wise man should not boast of it; he should think and not say "I am doing this." That is indeed the fourth quarter of brahmacharya.

sanskrit: evaṃ vasantaṃ yad upaplaved dhanam; ācāryāya tad anuprayacchet satāṃ vṛttiṃ bahuguṇām evam eti; guroḥ putre bhavati ca vṛttir eṣā
english: Whatever wealth accrues to one living thus — one should pass that on to the teacher. One thus acquires the conduct of the good with its many virtues; and this same conduct applies to the teacher's son.

sanskrit: evaṃ vasan sarvato vardhatīha; bahūn putrāṃl labhate ca pratiṣṭhām varṣanti cāsmai pradiśo diśaś ca; vasanty asmin brahmacarye janāś ca
english: One living thus grows in every direction here; he obtains many sons and renown. The quarters and directions rain blessings upon him, and people dwell within this brahmacharya of his.

sanskrit: etena brahmacaryeṇa devā devatvam āpnuvan ṛṣayaś ca mahābhāgā brahmalokaṃ manīṣiṇaḥ
english: By this brahmacharya the gods attained divinity, and the greatly fortunate sages, the wise ones, attained the world of Brahman.

sanskrit: gandharvāṇām anenaiva rūpam apsarasām abhūt etena brahmacaryeṇa sūryo ahnāya jāyate
english: By this very brahmacharya came the beauty of the Gandharvas and the Apsaras. By this brahmacharya the sun is born anew each day.

sanskrit: ya āśayet pāṭayec cāpi rājan; sarvaṃ śarīraṃ tapasā tapyamānaḥ etenāsau bālyam atyeti vidvān; mṛtyuṃ tathā rodhayaty antakāle
english: One who lies on the ground and burns the entire body with austerity, O king — by this brahmacharya the wise man transcends childhood and likewise holds back death at the hour of death.

sanskrit: antavantaḥ kṣatriya te jayanti; lokāñ janāḥ karmaṇā nirmitena brahmaiva vidvāṃs tena abhyeti sarvaṃ; nānyaḥ panthā ayanāya vidyate
english: Those worlds that men win through finite deeds are finite, O kshatriya. But the wise man attains Brahman itself through brahmacharya, the whole of it. There is no other path for going there.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca ābhāti śuklam iva lohitam iva; atho kṛṣṇam athāñjanaṃ kādravaṃ vā tad brāhmaṇaḥ paśyati yo 'tra vidvān; kathaṃrūpaṃ tad amṛtam akṣaraṃ padam
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Does it appear white, or red, or dark, or like collyrium, or tawny — what the knowledgeable brahmana sees who is skilled in this? What form has that immortal, imperishable state?

sanskrit: sanatsujāta uvāca nābhāti śuklam iva lohitam iva; atho kṛṣṇam āyasam arkavarṇam na pṛthivyāṃ tiṣṭhati nāntarikṣe; naitat samudre salilaṃ bibharti
english: Sanatsujata said: It does not appear white, nor red, nor dark, nor like iron, nor sun-colored. It does not abide on the earth, nor in the atmosphere. The ocean does not hold it in its waters.

sanskrit: na tārakāsu na ca vidyud āśritaṃ; na cābhreṣu dṛśyate rūpam asya na cāpi vāyau na ca devatāsu; na tac candre dṛśyate nota sūrye
english: It does not reside in the stars, nor in lightning. Its form is not seen in the clouds, nor in the wind, nor among the gods. It is not seen in the moon, nor in the sun.

sanskrit: naivarkṣu tan na yajuḥṣu nāpy atharvasu; na caiva dṛśyaty amaleṣu sāmasu rathaṃtare bārhate cāpi rājan; mahāvrate naiva dṛśyed dhruvaṃ tat
english: It is not in the Rig verses, nor in the Yajus, nor in the Atharvans. It is not seen even in the pure Sāmans, nor in the Rathantara or Bṛhatsāman, O king. Even in the Great Vow it cannot surely be seen.

sanskrit: apāraṇīyaṃ tamasaḥ parastāt; tad antako 'py eti vināśakāle aṇīyarūpaṃ kṣuradhārayā tan; mahac ca rūpaṃ tv api parvatebhyaḥ
english: It is beyond crossing over, beyond darkness. Even death reaches it at the time of dissolution. Its form is subtler than the edge of a razor, yet its form is greater than the mountains.

sanskrit: sā pratiṣṭhā tad amṛtaṃ lokās tad brahma tad yaśaḥ bhūtāni jajñire tasmāt pralayaṃ yānti tatra ca
english: That is the foundation, that is the immortal, those are the worlds, that is Brahman, that is glory. Beings were born from that, and to that they return at dissolution.

sanskrit: anāmayaṃ tan mahad udyataṃ yaśo; vāco vikārān kavayo vadanti tasmiñ jagat sarvam idaṃ pratiṣṭhitaṃ; ye tad vidur amṛtās te bhavanti
english: That is free from affliction, that great and exalted glory — the poets call it a transformation of speech. In that, all this universe is established. Those who know that become immortal.
